items.title: Beyond memory loss: recognising dementia in primary care
items.summary: An estimated one third of older people with dementia in England remain undiagnosed. Rachel Daly, academy lead Admiral Nurse at Dementia UK, explains how primary care nurses are well placed to recognise the patterns that point to the condition and make timely referrals. Dementia rarely presents as a direct concern.

items.summary: Although the number of people diagnosed with dementia is increasing globally, it is estimated that only 2% are engaged in dementia research in the UK. items.title: Recognising constipation in older residents with colostomies: practical guidance for nursing and residential care staff
items.summary: Constipation is a common but often under-recognised problem among older adults living in residential and nursing care settings. A persistent misconception exists that people with a colostomy cannot become constipated because faecal output is diverted through a stoma.
